classification.difficultyReason: Reproduce the demonstrated diagonal angle-bisection proof with relabelled vertices, choosing matching SSS triangles and stating the corresponding angle consequence.

content.prompt:
In the diagram to the right, $XYZW$ is a rhombus.

Prove that $XZ$ bisects $\angle X$ as presented earlier.

spec.description: Rhombus XYZW with X lower left, Y upper left, Z upper right and W lower right. Every side has one equality tick. XY and WZ have matching single parallel arrows; YZ and XW have matching double arrows. Both diagonals are dashed red. Ordinary source-blue geometry is rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: XY=YZ=ZW=WX; XY parallel to WZ; YZ parallel to XW; diagonals XZ and YW.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no angle-bisection marks or proof conclusions are supplied.

answer.short:
$\angle YXZ=\angle WXZ$, so $XZ$ bisects $\angle X$.

Triangles $XYZ$ and $XWZ$ are congruent by SSS.
answer.worked:
In triangles $XYZ$ and $XWZ$:
$$\begin{align*}XY&=XW &&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\YZ&=WZ &&\text{(sides of a rhombus)}\\XZ&=XZ &&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $\triangle XYZ\equiv\triangle XWZ$ (SSS).

Hence, $\angle YXZ=\angle WXZ$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

Therefore, $XZ$ bisects $\angle X$.
